builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: PrivacyPR: A Dataset of Real-World Privacy Fixes for Benchmarking Privacy-Aware Code Review
summary: PrivacyPR replaces ad-hoc or synthetic evaluation of privacy-aware code review with 4,131 real merged GitHub PRs linking actual privacy defects to accepted fixes, including a verified 250+250 split and a 100+100 evaluation subset with a harness that reverts fixes to reintroduce defects. Adoption costs evaluation compute against a hosted or local coding agent plus LLM-judge calls, fitting a single 24 GB GPU or third-party API budget, but requires building prompting and parsing around the provided harness. It can fail through LLM-generated labels with only 72% annotator endorsement, reverting-based defect reintroduction that may not compile or reproduce the original flaw, and high false-positive rates (11-15%) that make raw detector output noisy in production review pipelines.
rationale: A small team deploying coding agents for review can use the public Small split and harness at low cost to measure whether their own prompts and models catch GDPR-relevant defects before trusting the agent in production.
technique: PrivacyPR benchmark for privacy-aware code review agents

claims.statement: PrivacyPR replaces ad-hoc or synthetic evaluation of privacy-aware code review with 4,131 real merged GitHub PRs linking actual privacy defects to accepted fixes, including a verified 250+250 split and a 100+100 evaluation subset with a harness that reverts fixes to reintroduce defects. Adoption costs evaluation compute against a hosted or local coding agent plus LLM-judge calls, fitting a single 24 GB GPU or third-party API budget, but requires building prompting and parsing around the provided harness. It can fail through LLM-generated labels with only 72% annotator endorsement, reverting-based defect reintroduction that may not compile or reproduce the original flaw, and high false-positive rates (11-15%) that make raw detector output noisy in production review pipelines.

On the Small split, coding agents detect 42-51% of reintroduced privacy defects under a generic review prompt versus 88-91% under an explicit privacy-focused prompt, with 11-15% false positives on non-fix PRs; annotators endorsed 72% of the LLM's GDPR-principle labels on the Verified split.
